report.source_text: On examination in the emergency room, heart rate was 118 bpm, respiratory rate was 43 bpm and Glasgow Coma Scale was 10 without any focal neurological deficit. On laboratory testing, serum glucose was 628 mg/dL (70–140 mg/dL), beta-hydroxybutyrate was 2.3 mmol/L (0–0.5 mmol/L), white cell count was 12 300×109/L (3400–9600×109/L), platelet count 65×109/ L (157–371×109/ L), pH 7.04 (7.35–7.45), bicarbonate 8 mmol/L (22–26 mmol/L), anion gap 26 (7–15), D-dimer 2264 ng/mL (<500 ng/mL), fibrinogen >1000 mg/dL (200–393 mg/dL). Lactate was 1.1 (0.5–2.2 mmol/L), troponin was 6 ng/L (<10 ng/L), then <6 ng/L after 2 hours. Pregnancy test with quantitative human chorionic gonadotropin was negative at 0.7 IU/L (<5 IU/L). Plasma ethanol, acetaminophen and salicylate levels were negative. Serum ethanol, acetone, isopropanol and methanol levels were negative. Urine drug screen and volatile screen were negative.

clinician.final_diagnosis: an unusual and fulminant case of cerebral oedema in the setting of COVID-19 infection with bacterial infection, DKA and CVST
clinician.trajectory_summary: A woman in her 30s was admitted with diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA), COVID-19 infection, and altered mental status including confusion and agitation. Initial head CT was normal. Lab tests showed hyperglycemia, acidosis, thrombocytopenia, elevated white cells, and high D-dimer. Brain MRI and MR venography within hours demonstrated diffuse cerebral edema and cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVST). Blood cultures grew Klebsiella pneumoniae, treated with antibiotics. Treatment included remdesivir, dexamethasone, tocilizumab, and enoxaparin. On ICU day 2, head CT angiography showed worsening diffuse cerebral edema, new brainstem (Duret) hemorrhages, and progression of venous sinus thrombosis. The patient was declared brain dead soon thereafter, confirming fulminant cerebral edema and severe neurologic deterioration.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Initial labs confirmed DKA with hyperglycemia, acidosis, inflammation and prothrombotic markers (E001)
Head CT on presentation was negative for intracranial abnormality (initial presentation summary)
Brain MR venography demonstrated diffuse cerebral oedema and thrombosis of the dural venous sinuses and deep venous system (E009)
Blood cultures positive for Klebsiella pneumoniae, indicating bacterial infection (E008)
Treatment included remdesivir, dexamethasone, tocilizumab and enoxaparin anticoagulation (E007)
ICU day 2 head CT angiography showed worsening cerebral edema, new brainstem hemorrhages and progression of venous sinus thrombosis (E012)
The patient was declared brain dead soon after ICU day 2 imaging (E012)
